title: When the Safehouse Breaks
premise: Felix Delacroix, a deniable hostage negotiator haunted by the one exchange that ended in blood, discovers his own safe house listed on a real estate site — interior photos included, down to the case files he keeps in a floor safe. Someone inside the network sold him out. As Felix traces the leak through three governments' overlapping black operations, he is hunted by an assassin who turns out to be the sister of the hostage Felix failed to save years ago. In the end, Felix chooses exposure over survival: he releases the files publicly, dismantling the program and himself with it, and walks into custody as the assassin, justice satisfied differently than she planned, lets him live.
about_author: Edmund Halloran is a former crisis-line counselor who spent a decade listening to negotiations go wrong from the other end of a phone. He writes thrillers about people whose jobs require them to be nobody.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Scrolling property sites at 3 a.m., Felix finds his safe house for sale — twelve photos, including his floor safe half-open. He burns what he can carry and runs. Emotional beat: cold dread; the illusion of invisibility shattering in real time.

chapters.title: Handler of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Felix contacts his handler, Marek, who denies everything too quickly and offers him a new identity he didn't ask for. POV shifts briefly to Marek, revealing he knew about the listing days ago. Emotional beat: betrayal seeded; trust curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: Twelve Photographs
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Analyzing the photos, he realizes the camera angle could only come from inside the program — someone used surveillance footage as staging shots. He identifies a watermark linking to a private security firm serving all three governments. Emotional beat: methodical fear sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Woman at the Open House
chapters.summary: Assassin Ilsa Voss's POV. Posing as a buyer, she tours the emptying safe house and confirms Felix's habits from the dust patterns. She isn't hired to kill him yet — only to find him. Her motive: her brother died in Felix's failed negotiation. Emotional beat: grief weaponized.

chapters.title: Three Flags
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. In Vienna he meets a retired archivist who explains the program's structure: three governments sharing deniable assets, each able to burn the others. The listing was a message between agencies — and Felix is the collateral. Emotional beat: vertigo at the scale of the machine around him.

chapters.title: Negotiation of One
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Cornered in a train station, Felix does what he does best: negotiates — with Ilsa, face to face, buying six hours by promising her the truth about her brother. Both know it's a lie neither believes. Emotional beat: two predators circling, grudging recognition.

chapters.title: What the Safe Held
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Reading the recovered file on her brother's death, she learns the negotiation wasn't Felix's failure — his own agency sabotaged the exchange to protect a source. Her target shifts upward. Emotional beat: rage redirected; the ground of her vengeance collapsing.

chapters.title: The Sale Closes
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Marek sells him out formally — a termination order dressed as extraction. Felix survives the ambush using the safe house's own layout against the team, then broadcasts the files to three dead-drop journalists simultaneously. Emotional beat: cornered animal becoming the threat.

chapters.title: Every Door Opens
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The files detonate across three capitals; agencies scramble to disown the program while hunting its ghosts. Ilsa has one clear shot at Felix and takes it — deliberately wide. Emotional beat: chaos as liberation; the moment vengeance becomes choice.

chapters.title: Attribution
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Instead of vanishing again, Felix surrenders publicly, testifying under his real name — the name he buried for fifteen years. Justice outside the law cost him everything except himself. Final beat: quiet, hard-won peace; identity reclaimed at last.
